headline: Revenue grows, impairment and buybacks reshape earnings
summary_short: Bright Horizons' Q2 2026 revenue rose 7% y/y to $779.2 million as back-up care grew 19%, but a $19.1 million impairment charge drove GAAP net income down 26% to $40.6 million even as adjusted diluted EPS climbed 20% to $1.28.
summary_long: Revenue grew 7% y/y to $779.2 million, led by 19% growth in back-up care and continued full-service growth, partly offset by revenue lost from centers closed over the trailing 12 months. GAAP operating income fell 7% to $79.8 million and net income fell 26% to $40.6 million, both driven by a $19.1 million impairment charge on underperforming centers, a higher effective tax rate, and higher interest expense. Excluding the impairment, adjusted income from operations rose 15% to $99.0 million and adjusted diluted EPS grew 20% to $1.28. The company repurchased $473.2 million of stock in H1 and amended its credit facility, raising revolver capacity to $1.0 billion. FY2026 guidance: revenue $3.085-$3.115 billion, adjusted diluted EPS $5.05-$5.15.

drivers.explanation: Growth driven by back-up care revenue (+19% y/y) and full-service center-based child care growth, partially offset by revenue lost from centers closed over the trailing 12 months.

Gross profit rose as revenue's dollar increase ($47.6M) exceeded cost of services' dollar increase ($41.2M); gross margin still narrowed to 24.3% from 25.0% since costs grew slightly faster in percentage terms.
Decrease primarily related to $19.1 million of impairment losses on centers in certain markets, partially offset by increased service levels and back-up care segment contributions.
Decline reflects the drop in operating income noted above, plus a higher effective tax rate and higher interest expense.
Y/y decline tracks the 26% net income decline, partly offset by a lower diluted share count (51.8M vs 57.7M) from continued buybacks; q/q increase mirrors the sequential net income rebound.
Cash fell y/y as $473.2 million of first-half share repurchases and financing outflows exceeded the $202.8 million of operating cash generated, despite proceeds from a new term loan.
Debt rose after the company amended its credit facility on June 1, 2026, issuing a new $375 million term loan A facility and raising revolver capacity to $1.0 billion.
Equity fell as roughly $471.5 million of treasury stock repurchases during the first half reduced equity by more than net income added to it.

CEO cited solid 7% revenue growth and 20% adjusted EPS growth, with back-up care revenue outpacing overall growth and full-service margin expansion; the release also gave FY2026 revenue and adjusted diluted EPS guidance.
